summary: Mostly a type-level refactor of the @cipherstash/stack encryption client: twelve `as never` forwarding casts are removed, the native client's `encryptQuery` takes a tuple-union argument list, and the encrypt operations accept the v3 Json document type. The one intentional public-contract change is that `EncryptionClient.encrypt` on a `types.Json` column now types `data` as `Encrypted | null`, which matches the existing runtime behaviour (a null document already resolved to `{ data: null }`). It ships as a minor bump. The runtime changes are small. `NativeEncryptionClient.encryptQuery` now branches on `args[1]` instead of `opts`, which is equivalent. The stack-supabase per-term fallback now throws on a null envelope instead of sending the string "null". That path runs only when a client has no `bulkEncrypt`, and null operands are filtered out before encryption. Head CI is green, including the stack/supabase/drizzle type tests, the Node and Bun unit tests and the Drizzle v3 integration jobs, which run the new live json-crypto null-element round trips. The residual risk is compile-time breakage for downstream TypeScript consumers, which is loud and documented.

behaviour_changes.description:
`EncryptionClient.encrypt` gains a third type parameter `P` (default: the column's plaintext type) and returns `EncryptOperation>`, where `EncryptResult

= Encrypted | (null & P)`. For a `types.Json` column (whose document type admits null) the success `data` is now typed `Encrypted | null`; scalar columns are unchanged. `EncryptResult` is newly exported. Type-only: runtime already returned null for a null plaintext.

Exported operation classes (`EncryptOperation`, `EncryptOperationWithLockContext`, `EncryptQueryOperation`, `BatchEncryptQueryOperation`, `BulkEncryptOperation`) widen constructor and `getOperation()` plaintext types from `Plaintext` to internal `PlaintextInput` (`Plaintext | JsonDocument`); `EncryptOperation` gains an optional result type parameter defaulting to `Encrypted`.

Native `encryptQuery` takes `...args: EncryptQueryArgs` and discriminates on `args[1]` instead of a named `opts`; the typed client forwards with `...args` instead of always passing two (cast) arguments. Runtime branching is equivalent: `args[1]` is the same value `opts` was. A scalar without options no longer type-checks (it threw at runtime before).

stack-supabase `encryptGroupPerTerm` (used only when the encryption client has no `bulkEncrypt`) now throws `EncryptionFailedError` when `encrypt` resolves to a null envelope, instead of JSON-stringifying it to "null" and sending it as the filter operand. Matches the existing bulk path.

Six scattered `as JsPlaintext` casts replaced by one `toJsPlaintext` helper (an identity function with a type assertion); model encrypt results narrowed by two explicit assertions in client-v3 instead of `as never`. No runtime change.
The shipped `stash-encryption` agent skill now documents that `encrypt(null)` on a Json column resolves to `{ data: null }` with `data` typed `Encrypted | null`.

failure_scenarios.title: Minor release breaks downstream TypeScript builds that dereference Json encrypt results
failure_scenarios.trigger: A consumer upgrades @cipherstash/stack across the minor version and has code like `const r = await client.encrypt(doc, { table, column: t.jsonCol }); r.data.c` where `doc` is typed `JsonDocument`, or names `ReturnType<EncryptionClient['encrypt']>`.
failure_scenarios.mechanism:
`encrypt` now returns `EncryptOperation>` with `EncryptResult

= Encrypted | (null & P)`; `JsonDocument` admits null, so `data` becomes `Encrypted | null` and strict-null code fails with TS18047. The default `P` keeps explicit `` calls compiling but types them `Encrypted | null` for Json columns.
failure_scenarios.consequence: Compile errors in consumer builds after a minor bump (loud, caught before deploy). Runtime behaviour is unchanged, and the code these errors flag already threw at runtime when the document was null.

existing_verification.description: Type tests pinning encrypt's result type (literal null, JsonDocument, non-null, scalar, lock context, audit, explicit type args) run in the stack `test:types` step of Run Tests (Node 22/24), which passed on head.

missing_verification: No check against external consumer code; the semver classification (minor for a type narrowing that can break compilation) is a judgement call.
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Keep the changeset text that tells users to null-check `result.data` for Json columns, and make sure the release notes put it first.

failure_scenarios.title: Supabase per-term fallback now fails queries it previously sent
failure_scenarios.trigger: A Supabase builder is given an encryption client without `bulkEncrypt` (older or custom client) and some query operand encrypts to a null envelope.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: `encryptGroupPerTerm` throws `EncryptionFailedError` on `result.data === null` (query-encrypt.ts:417-421). Null and `is` operands are skipped before encryption (query-terms.ts:180), so this fires only on a contract violation by the client.
failure_scenarios.consequence: A query that previously sent the string "null" as the filter operand, and so silently matched the wrong rows, now returns an error. This moves from silent wrong results to a loud failure.

existing_verification.description: New unit test 'rejects a null envelope on the per-term fallback rather than sending "null"' in supabase-v3-builder.test.ts. Unit test jobs passed on head, but the logs are not available to confirm that this file ran in them.

failure_scenarios.mitigation: None needed beyond the changeset note; behaviour now matches the bulk path.

evidence.claim:
EncryptResult

= Encrypted | (null & P) defines the new result type.
EncryptionClient.encrypt now has a defaulted P type parameter and returns EncryptOperation>.
At base, encrypt returned plain EncryptOperation (data typed Encrypted).
At base, a null plaintext already returned null at runtime (`null as unknown as Encrypted`), so BC-1 is type-only.
PlaintextInput = Plaintext | JsonDocument, used to widen the operation classes' inputs.
Native encryptQuery branches on args[1] / args[0] with the same logic as the base opts / plaintextOrTerms.
Typed client forwards encryptQuery with ...args (base passed two `as never` args).
Per-term fallback throws on a null envelope.
Unit test asserts the per-term fallback returns 500 with 'null envelope at position 0'.
toJsPlaintext is an identity function with a type assertion.
Model encrypt results are narrowed by two explicit assertions instead of `as never`.
Skill text updated to describe encrypt(null) on Json columns returning { data: null } typed Encrypted | null.
`is` predicates and null operands are forwarded unencrypted, so null never reaches encryptGroupPerTerm via normal filters.
PR and changeset state code reading result.data after encrypting a possibly-null Json value must now check for null; released as a minor bump.
